stimulus: A building contractor recorded the masses of 40 bags of cement in a delivery. The histogram shows the results. A bag is accepted if its mass lies within one estimated semi-interquartile range of the estimated median mass.
stem: Use the histogram to answer the questions below.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the class width for the interval $40 \le m < 50$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the mean mass of a bag of cement.

parts.label: c
parts.statement: The median class is {}. The estimated median mass is {} kg. The distribution is {}.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Complete the statement below. Give numerical estimates correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.statement: The estimated interquartile range is {} kg and the estimated semi-interquartile range is {} kg. A bag weighing $58$ kg is {}.

rubric.hint: Subtract the lower class boundary from the upper class boundary to find the class width in kg.
Find each class midpoint by averaging the two boundaries of that class.
Multiply every class midpoint by its frequency and add the products to calculate $\sum fx$.

rubric.criterion: Divides by total frequency to obtain $1900 \div 40 = 47.5$.
rubric.template: Divides by total frequency to obtain $1900 \div 40 = {b.i}$.
rubric.hint: Divide your weighted total by the total frequency using $\text{weighted total} \div \text{total frequency}$.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the 20th value and the median class $40 \le m < 50$.
rubric.template: Identifies the 20th value and the median class $40 \le m < 50$.
rubric.hint: Find the halfway observation from the total frequency, then identify its class and write the boundaries as lower boundary $\le m <$ upper boundary.
Interpolate within the median class by adding the lower boundary to $\frac{\text{position into class}}{\text{class frequency}}\times\text{class width}$.

rubric.criterion: Compares their estimated mean and median to conclude that the distribution is approximately symmetrical.
rubric.template: Compares their estimated mean and median to conclude that the distribution is approximately symmetrical.
rubric.hint: Compare your estimated mean with your estimated median and use how close they are to state whether the distribution is approximately symmetrical.

rubric.criterion: Identifies quartile positions as the 10th and 30th values.
rubric.template: Identifies quartile positions as the 10th and 30th values.
rubric.hint: Find the observations one quarter and three quarters of the way through the total frequency.
Interpolate in the two quartile classes and record the estimates as $Q_1 \approx \ldots$ and $Q_3 \approx \ldots$.

rubric.criterion: Uses their quartiles to calculate interquartile range and semi-interquartile range.
rubric.template: Uses their quartiles to calculate interquartile range and semi-interquartile range.
rubric.hint: Subtract your lower quartile from your upper quartile, then divide this interquartile range by two to find the semi-interquartile range.

rubric.criterion: Expresses the estimated semi-interquartile range correct to 1 decimal place.
rubric.template: Expresses the estimated semi-interquartile range correct to 1 decimal place.
rubric.hint: Round your estimated semi-interquartile range to one decimal place.

rubric.criterion: Uses their estimated median plus or minus their semi-interquartile range to decide that $58$ kg is not acceptable.
rubric.template: Uses their estimated median plus or minus their semi-interquartile range to decide that $58$ kg is not acceptable.
rubric.hint: Use your estimated median plus or minus your semi-interquartile range to form the acceptable interval, compare the bag mass with it, and state that the bag is not acceptable.

final_answer: $10$ kg; $47.5$ kg; $40 \le m < 50$; $47.5$; approximately symmetrical; $19.2$; $9.6$; not acceptable
worked_solution:
(a) The class width is $50-40=10$ kg.

(b) The class midpoints are $25,35,45,55,65$. The weighted total is
\[
(25\times4)+(35\times7)+(45\times12)+(55\times9)+(65\times8)=1900.
\]
The total frequency is $40$, giving an estimated mean of $1900\div40=47.5$ kg.

(c) The median position is $\frac{40}{2}=20$. The cumulative frequencies are $4,11,23,32,40$, so the median class is $40\le m<50$. The estimated median is
\[
40+\left(\frac{20-11}{12}\right)\times10=47.5\text{ kg}.
\]
The estimated mean and estimated median are both $47.5$ kg, so the distribution is approximately symmetrical.

(d) The lower-quartile position is $\frac{40}{4}=10$ and the upper-quartile position is $\frac{3\times40}{4}=30$. The estimated lower quartile is
\[
30+\left(\frac{10-4}{7}\right)\times10=38.6\text{ kg} \text{ approximately}.
\]
The estimated upper quartile is
\[
50+\left(\frac{30-23}{9}\right)\times10=57.8\text{ kg} \text{ approximately}.
\]
Therefore, the estimated interquartile range is $57.8-38.6=19.2$ kg and the estimated semi-interquartile range is $19.2\div2=9.6$ kg. The acceptable interval is approximately $47.5\pm9.6$, or from $37.9$ kg to $57.1$ kg. Since $58$ kg is outside this interval, the bag is not acceptable.

misconceptions.name: Modal frequency given as the mean
misconceptions.remediation: The value 12 is the greatest frequency, not a mass estimate. For grouped data, multiply each class midpoint by its frequency and divide the total by 40.

misconceptions.name: Range reported as an interval
misconceptions.remediation: The interquartile range is one number. Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile: $57.8-38.6=19.2$ kg.
